scenario: [LINT.7.2]: a `null` endpoint does not make an interval invalid, and [RLOW.6.1.7]: a pair with a `null` endpoint is valid. One N with `t` 1 and `b` 3 and no `a`: rule `inside` tests `n.t in (n.a .. n.b)`, whose comparison is `null` ([LNUL.4.1]), so it does not fire and nothing faults; rule `handler` never fires. Rule `seen` fires and logs `seen 1`, so the vector cannot pass with nothing run. A check that treated the `null` start as failing `s <= e` would raise DOMAIN and `handler` would log. PATH PINNED: FN_INTERVAL_CHECK skipping a pair with a `null` endpoint, in libds `eval_interval_check` (rete/eval.c) and Mercury `ds.eval.rlow_6_1_7_interval_check`.
rules_ds:
schema N scope logical:
    id: Int key
    t: Int mutable
    a: Int? mutable
    b: Int mutable

rule inside:
    N n where n.t in (n.a .. n.b)
->
    log info "inside {n.id}"

rule seen:
    N n
->
    log info "seen {n.id}"

rule handler:
    ComputationError e
->
    log critical "{e.kind} [{e.schema}] [{e.slot}]"
